always.01: Some claims are true for every value and stand before anyone arrives. The Margin calls one an always, and finds them faintly embarrassing, and builds on them anyway.

bell.01: The Bell hangs beneath Leaf One and rings once for every leaf that stops being true. It has rung thirty-seven times this year. Nobody has ever had to be told what it means.

bollard.01: The arch at the head of this leaf and the arch above the certainty field are the two ends of one animal. A surveyor settled that four generations ago, to general agreement and no particular interest. Nobody changed the names, because the names are useful, and nobody has settled anything else about it since. It has perhaps eighty years of leaf left to cross.

carrywren.01: Carrywrens drink from the carries and consequently fly slightly faster than they are.

circuit.01: The Ninth Circuit runs eleven Provisionals over forty leaves and keeps a depot on none of them. You will meet two.

cutters.01: Cutters do not say the word "I" during a cut. Ask one why and they will show you a hand.

edgewake.01: Pilgrims come to the lip to count the towers of Vantis. No two counts have ever agreed. The Edgewake consider this the finding, not the failure.

flatleaf.01: Leaf Two Hundred and Six is a single claim the size of a leaf, and it is the largest true statement in the Margin, and it is a floor, and nobody knows what it was the floor of.

hush.01: A hush eats grey. Where one has grazed, an approximate wall is simply not there any more, and the hole is honest. The Sufficiency has a form for this and files it under weather.

leafninealso.01: Leaf Nine Also broke off Leaf Nine eleven hundred years ago and kept the name. Both claims are under review. The Sufficiency has offered to widen the name.

mark.01: A gate set to a mark does not stand level and is not supposed to. It leans toward whatever it lets through, and a gate that has stopped leaning has stopped admitting anybody.

nearlies.01: Carries flow toward whatever is nearly true, so the Nearlies bait their lines with sentences they deliberately do not finish. A half-sayer who completes one at the weir buys the drinks.

hundred.01: Leaf Forty is held aloft by nine hundred people singing in shifts. They have not stopped in six generations. Their shift change is a public holiday.

refusal.01: A claim no value will close is called a refusal. The name of Leaf Nine is one: two leaves hold it, no value settles it, and the Sufficiency has offered to widen the name.

remainder.01: The Remainder still stands because its claim was written so badly nobody has managed to make it false either.

sagsmith.01: A sagsmith cannot close a claim and does not pretend to. He props. Every grey roof in the Margin stands on somebody's stacked certainties and somebody's patience.

several.01: A several has never been counted, so the Margin gave up and changed the grammar instead: a several are. Part of one being on the far side of a leaf does not make it two, and the surveyors who argued otherwise are the reason the word exists.

solvary.01: The Solvary is understaffed by about nine thousand. It has never turned anyone away; it simply has nobody to spare to stand beside you while you close your first one.

stray.01: A stray is an unknown that has slipped its claim. It cannot be rounded while it stays unsolved, which means the safest possible life for a stray is one in which it is never anything at all.

rounded.01: A stray rounded all the way down is not destroyed. It becomes a value: definite, permanent, filed. Nobody in the Margin calls this a death, and that is the part people find difficult.

tare.01: The Tare fly on a claim about their own mass, which is why they know the weight of everything they own, including their boots, including you. A Tare funeral is a subtraction.

thousandfoot.01: No thousandfoot has ever been counted twice with the same result. Three surveyors have retired over this.

tolerance.01: The Tolerance is a mark, and a mark is a claim like any other, which makes it the largest standing claim in the Margin. It is posted rather than announced, and revised rather than decided.

warden.01: A Warden is the Fifth Rung, and the Fifth Rung is the one where a person may set a mark of their own. Until the Solvary made the Rung there was exactly one body in the Margin that could, and it is still the one doing it.
